chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who joins two chapters (surahs) in one bowing (rak'ah). He said: 'Indeed, every chapter has a right, so give each its right from the bowing and prostration.' I said: 'And if he cuts (interrupts) the chapter?' He said: 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.حَقّاً: a right (obligatory due to the surah)
key_terms.يَقْرُنُ: joins/combines (referring to reciting two surahs in one rak'ah)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to join two Quranic chapters in one rak'ah of prayer, and what is the ruling if a surah is interrupted?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the ideal practice of completing a surah's recitation before bowing and the permissibility of interrupting it to join another, reflecting the Shia juristic view that while each surah has a 'right' to be fully recited, cutting it does not invalidate the prayer. This ruling underscores the flexibility in *Sunnah* recitations during obligatory prayers, prioritizing the structural integrity of the rak'ah over strict adherence to continuous recitation. The emphasis on 'giving each surah its right' highlights the spiritual weight attributed to Quranic recitation in Shia devotional practice.
